      WHEREAS, the Office of Emergency Management within the Department of Public Safety ("OEM") is committed to providing efficient and effective Citizens' Emergency Alert System to the City of Newark ("City") and its citizens; and 
      
      WHEREAS, pursuant to Local Public Contracts Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-5(1)(dd), a contract for proprietary computer software may be awarded without advertising and public bidding therefor if the contract is for the provision or performance of goods or services for the support or maintenance of proprietary computer hardware and software; and
      	
      WHEREAS,  OEM desires to enter into a contract with Rave Wireless, Inc. ("Rave Wireless"), 492 Old Connecticut Path, Framingham, Massachusetts 01701, for the provision, maintenance and support of the Citizens' Emergency Alert System, which is Rave Wireless's proprietary software; and
      
      WHEREAS, said contract is essential for the conduct of the affairs of the OEM, as said proprietary software and hardware includes, Fully hosted platform operated on the Rave Alert for Public Safety,  NDN(tm) telecom network, Customizable contact management, Unlimited system users, Voice (Recorded or Text-to-Speech with TTY/TDD), Email, Fax, Pager, Social Media, RSS, IPAWS, GIS Mapping, Special Events Manager, NWS Automated Weather Alerts, Rave Mobile  provided Voice Add-On Module, Premium SMS Messaging, Social Media Integration, CAP inbound/outbound, Geopolling, SMS Opt-In, Inbound 800 Service, Smart Loader, Loaded Landlines, Conference Blast, and Rave Prepare live customer support and unlimited live webinar training for use by the City's essential Departments and agencies; and 
      
      WHEREAS, Rave Wireless has represented that it has the exclusive right to provide these goods or services, and the Coordinator of OEM certifies that said goods and services are essential and necessary for the conduct of the affairs of the Department of Public Safety, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-2(39); and
      
      WHEREAS, the annual cost of this service is expected to be Forty-Eight Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($48,000.00) each year for two (2) years, and should not exceed Ninety-Six Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($96,000.00) over that time period; and
      
      WHEREAS, the Coordinator of OEM has determined and certified in writing that the value of this contract will exceed $44,000.00; and
      
      WHEREAS, this contract is being awarded pursuant to a "Non-Fair and Open" Process pursuant to State Pay-to-Play Law, N.J.S.A.19:44A-20.5; and 
       
      WHEREAS, Rave Wireless has completed and submitted a Business Entity Disclosure Certification, which certifies that it has not made any reportable contributions to a political or candidate committee in the City of Newark in the previous one (1) year, and the contract will prohibit Rave Wireless from making any reportable contributions throughout the term of the contract; and
      
      WHEREAS, Rave Wireless and its subcontractors, if any, have certified that it and they are in compliance with the City's Contractor Pay-to-Play Reform Ordinance 2:4-22C.
 
      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NEWARK, NEW JERSEY, THAT:

1. The Mayor and/or his designee, the Business Administrator or the Director of the Department of Public Safety, are authorized to enter into and execute a contract with Rave Wireless, Inc., 492 Old Connecticut Path, Framingham, Massachusetts 01701, to provide support and maintenance of proprietary software and hardware, which includes: Fully hosted platform operated on the Rave Alert for Public Safety,  NDN(tm) telecom network, Customizable contact management, Unlimited system users, Voice (Recorded or Text-to-Speech with TTY/TDD), Email, Fax, Pager, Social Media, RSS, IPAWS, GIS Mapping, Special Events Manager, NWS Automated Weather Alerts, Rave Mobile  provided Voice Add-On Module, Premium SMS Messaging, Social Media Integration, CAP inbound/outbound, Geopolling, SMS Opt-In, Inbound 800 Service, Smart Loader, Loaded Landlines, Conference Blast, and Rave Prepare live customer support and unlimited live webinar training for use by the City's essential Departments.   
                       
2. Said contract shall not exceed Ninety-Six Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($96,000.00) and shall be for the two year period commencing January 1, 2024 and ending on December 31, 2025.

3. This contract is ratified back from January 1, 2024 through the date of adoption of this authorizing Resolution.

4. Attached hereto is Finance Director's Certification of Funds  certifying that sufficient funds have been appropriated and are available for the purposes set forth in Paragraph 1. Funds shall be charged against the following account: Business Unit NW051, Dept. G23, Div./Proj. P23K0, Activity A, Account # 71280, Budget Ref B2023.  Funds for this contract shall be provided by the Urban Areas Security Initiative FY23 Grant. 

5. This contract is being awarded pursuant to the Non-Fair and Open Procedures of the State of New Jersey Pay-to-Play Law, (N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.5), the Local Public Contracts Law, (N.J.S.A. 40A:11-5(1)(dd), and the City of Newark's Contractor Pay-to-Play Reform Ordinance 2:4-22C. There shall be no advance payments made against this contract in accordance with N.J.S.A. 40A:5-16.

6. The Business Entity Disclosure Certification and the Determination of Value Letter are attached in support of this Resolution and shall be placed on file with the Office of the City Clerk by the Director of the Department of Finance.
 	
7. There shall be no amendments or changes to this contract without approval of the Municipal Council.

8. The contract will contain language prohibiting any contributions in violation of any State or local law.

9. A duly executed copy of the contract shall be filed in the Office of the City Clerk by the Coordinator of the Office of Emergency Management.

10. A notice of this action shall be published in a newspaper authorized by law to publish a legal advertisement and as required by law within ten (10) days of its passage.


STATEMENT

This Resolution ratifies and authorizes the Mayor and/or his designee, the Business Administrator or the Director of the Department of Public Safety, to enter into and execute a contract with Rave Wireless, Inc., 492 Old Connecticut Path, Framingham, Massachusetts 01701, for the provision of the Citizens' Emergency Alert Mass Notification System for an amount not to exceed $96,000.00, for a two (2) year period commencing January 1, 2024 and ending on December 31, 2025. This Resolution is ratified back to January 1, 2024.

	WHEREAS, the Office of the City Clerk is committed to providing efficient and effective means to process and maintain the City of Newark's legislation and best practices for the City's administrative and legislative branches in the performance of their duties with continued transparency while performing these functions; and 

	WHEREAS, the City Clerk, on behalf of the City of Newark desires to enter into a contract with Granicus, LLC, 1152 15th Street, Washington, DC 20005 to provide for the hosting, support, upgrades, maintenance and managed services of computer hardware and software of the system known as, Legistar the Legislative Management Software, a proprietary system, in order to maintain the software's operational health and functionality for an amount not to exceed Two Hundred Fifty-Five Thousand, Two Hundred and Five Dollars and Sixty Eight Cents ($255,205.68), for the period of February 1, 2024 through January 31, 2026; and

	WHEREAS, this support, maintenance and managed services contract is essential for the City Clerk to continue to provide a fully integrated Workflow and Agenda Management System for use by the Municipal Council and City Departments; and
	
	WHEREAS, Granicus, LLC, owns the rights to Legistar the Legislative Management Software System, and is engaged in the business of providing various "goods and services" ("...including any work, labor, commodities, equipment, materials or supplies of any tangible or intangible nature..." N.J.S.A. 40A:11-2 (24)) of the proprietary hardware and software; and 

	WHEREAS, Granicus, LLC, has represented that they are qualified, by their training and experience, to provide the required services and that they have the exclusive right to make and sell these goods and services, which the City Clerk certifies is essential and necessary for the conduct of its affairs, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-2(39); and 

	WHEREAS, pursuant to Local Public Contracts Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-5(1)(dd) such a contract for a proprietary computer system, may be awarded as an exception to public bidding because the provision or performance of goods and services is for the support and maintenance of proprietary computer hardware and software; and 

      WHEREAS, the City Clerk has determined and certified in writing that the value of this contract will exceed $17,500.00; and 
       
	WHEREAS, this contract is being awarded pursuant to a "Non-Fair and Open" Process, pursuant to State Pay-to-Play Law, N.J.S.A.19:44A-20.5; and

	WHEREAS, Granicus, LLC, has completed and submitted a Business Entity Disclosure Certification, which certifies that Granicus, LLC, has not made any contributions to a political or candidate committee in the previous one (1) year, and that the contract will prohibit Granicus, LLC, from making any contributions through the term of this contract; and
      
        WHEREAS, the Municipal Council adopted New Jersey Municipal Code � 2:4-22C.1, which adopted the State of New Jersey's Pay-to-Play statutory requirements pursuant to N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.5, as may be amended and supplemented, governing eligibility for municipal contracts; and
      
      WHEREAS, the Business Entity and its subcontractors, if any, have certified that it is in compliance with the aforementioned Municipal and State Pay-to-Play requirements.

	NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NEWARK, NEW JERSEY, THAT:

1.	The City Clerk is hereby authorized on behalf of the City of Newark to enter into and execute a contract with Granicus, LLC, 1152 15th Street, Washington, DC 20005, to provide the support and maintenance of the proprietary software, Legistar the Legislative Management Software, and associated services, in an amount not to exceed Two Hundred Fifty-Five Thousand, Two Hundred and Five Dollars and Sixty Eight Cents ($255,205.68), for the period of February 1, 2024 through January 31, 2026.

2.	Pursuant to N.J.A.C. 5:30-5(a), Temporary Budget, 2024 Adopted Budget, attached hereto is the Chief Finance Officer's Certification, which states partial funds in the amount of Thirty Thousand Dollars ($30,000.00) are available in the 2024 Budget, Business Unit NW011, Dept. 020, Div./Proj. 0201, Account #71280, the balance to be provided in the 2024 Adopted Budget. The Certification shall be filed, along with the original Resolution and the executed contract in the Office of the City Clerk.

3.	This contract is being awarded pursuant to and in compliance with the Non-Fair and Open Procedures of the Pay-to-Play Law, N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.5 et seq. and the Contractor-Pay-to-Play Ordinance, 2:4-22C, and as an exception to the Local Public Contracts Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-5 (dd) because these goods and services are for the support or maintenance of proprietary software and associated services.

4.	Granicus, LLC, has represented that they are qualified, by their training and experience, to provide the required services and that they have the exclusive right to make and sell these services, which the City Clerk certifies is essential and necessary for the conduct of its affairs N.J.S.A. 40A:11-2(39).

5.	The contract will contain language prohibiting any contributions in violation of any state or local law.

6.	That the Business Entity Disclosure Certification and the Determination of Value be placed on file with this Resolution.

7.	A copy of the executed contract herein authorized shall be filed in the Office of the City Clerk and shall be made available for public inspection.

	
STATEMENT

      This Resolution authorizes the City Clerk, on behalf of the City of Newark, to enter into and execute a contract with Granicus, LLC, 1152 15th Street, Washington, DC 20005, to provide for the hosting, support, upgrades, maintenance and managed services of computer hardware and software of the system known as, Legistar the Legislative Management Software, which is a proprietary system, in order to maintain the software's operational health and functionality, and associated services for a contract amount not to exceed $255,205.68, for the period of February 1, 2024 through January 31, 2026.

      WHEREAS, 54 Lockwood Street Urban Renewal, LLC, c/o Bridge Industrial, One Gatehall Drive, Suite 201, Parsippany, New Jersey 07054 filed an application with the Mayor seeking a long term tax abatement under the Long Term Tax Exemption Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:20-1 et seq. for a Twenty (20) year term for a project located in the East Ward at 54-56 Lockwood St., Newark, New Jersey and identified on the City's tax map as Block 2412, Lot 58 involving the demolition of the existing obsolete industrial buildings, environmental site remediation, and redevelopment of the land with construction of an approximately 211,388 square foot industrial distribution warehouse building consisting of approximately 26 loading docks, 2 drive in ramps, and 155 car parking spaces, all as further described in the Developer's Application, located at 54-56 Lockwood St., Newark, New Jersey and identified on the City's tax map as Block 2412, Lot 58 (collectively, the "Project"); and

      WHEREAS, the Mayor has submitted the application and proposed Financial Agreement to the Municipal Council with his recommendation thereof, a copy of which is annexed hereto; and

      WHEREAS, the Department of Economic and Housing Development has determined pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:20-11 that the relative benefits of this Project outweigh any costs associated with this tax exemption and that without the tax abatement granted herein, the Project would not be undertaken.

      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NEWARK, NEW JERSEY, THAT:

      1. The application of 54 Lockwood Street Urban Renewal, LLC, c/o Bridge Industrial, One Gatehall Drive, Suite 201, Parsippany, New Jersey 07054, seeking a long term tax abatement under the Long Term Tax Exemption Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:20-1 et seq. for a twenty (20) year term for a project located in the East Ward at 54-56 Lockwood St., Newark, New Jersey and identified on the City's tax map as Block 2412, Lot 58 involving the demolition of the existing obsolete industrial buildings, environmental site remediation, and redevelopment of the land with construction of an approximately 211,388 square foot industrial distribution warehouse building consisting of approximately 26 loading docks, 2 drive in ramps, and 155 car parking spaces (collectively, the "Project") is hereby approved in accordance with the recommendation of the Mayor.

      2. The abatement from taxation on improvements is hereby granted to the Entity for a period of twenty (20) years pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:20-12, and only so long as the Entity is subject to and complies with the proposed Financial Agreement and the Long Term Tax Exemption Law, as amended and supplemented.

      3. The Mayor of the City of Newark is hereby authorized to execute, on the City's behalf, the Financial Agreement in the form attached hereto.

      4. The Director shall file an executed copy of the Financial Agreement authorized by this ordinance in the Office of the City Clerk.

      5. The Project, when completed, will conform with all State laws and ordinances of the City of Newark relating to its construction and use.

      6. The Affirmative Action Program now on file in the Office of the City Clerk is declared to be a material condition of the Financial Agreement authorized by this ordinance.

      7. The Entity shall, in the operation of the Project, comply with all laws so that no person shall be subject to any discrimination because of race, religious principles, color, national origin, or ancestry.

      8. The Entity shall file an employment report (herein described below) with the Office of Affirmative Action, who shall forthwith, after receiving the report, send a copy thereof to the City Clerk, and the Office of Affirmative Action shall forthwith investigate the matters contained therein and report its findings to the Municipal Council.

      9. The annual service charge shall be based on the greater of the minimum annual service charge or 13.5% - 16.5% of the Total Project Costs as set forth more fully within the Financial Agreement.

      10. The Entity shall pay the minimum annual service charge, as calculated pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:20-12(b)(2)(e) and the Financial Agreement, in each year in which the annual service charge, as provided in paragraph 9 above, would be less than the minimum annual service charge.

      11. The following occurrences and requirements are express conditions of the granting of this tax abatement to be performed by the Entity, and the failure to comply with these requirements will result in the cancellation of the tax abatement:

            (a) The Entity shall not, without the prior consent of the Municipal Council of the City of Newark, sell, lease, assign, encumber, subordinate, convey, mortgage, or transfer all or any part of the Project so as to sever, disconnect or divide the improvements from the land embraced within the Project;

            (b) The Entity shall concomitantly, with the submission of the annual report required of it by N.J.S.A. 40A:20-9(d), attach an employment report under oath, with particulars, stating the manner and the extent to which it has complied with paragraph 8 above.  This employment report shall be filed with the Director of Finance, the City Clerk, and the Director of the Department of Economic and Housing Development;

            (c) The Entity shall pay all outstanding taxes and all outstanding water and sewer charges within thirty (30) days of the adoption of this ordinance;

            (d) The Entity shall submit to the City a copy of its formation documents, as approved by the Department of Community Affairs and filed with the Secretary of State;

            (e) The Entity shall receive a favorable review and certification from the appropriate City departments and agencies, pursuant to City Ordinance 6S&Fd, adopted October 21, 1992, as amended.

      12. That in any year that the Entity shall fail to make four (4) consecutive land tax payments when due and owing in the manner defined in N.J.S.A. 40A:20-12(b)(2)(e), such delinquency shall render the Entity ineligible for any land tax credits against the annual service charge.

      13. The Entity understands and agrees that the revenue projections set forth in the application are estimates and that the actual payments in lieu of taxes to be paid by the Entity to the City shall be determined pursuant to the Financial Agreement to be executed between the Entity and the City of Newark. 

      14. To the extent of any inconsistency with any prior City ordinance and/or Municipal Code provision governing the granting of long-term tax exemptions, including, inter alia, procedures for application, review and approval, required terms of the financial agreement, required conditions and covenants, limits on duration, means of enforcement, and all other matters whatsoever, such prior City ordinances and/or Municipal Code provisions are hereby waived, but only with respect to this ordinance.

      15. Within ten (10) calendar days following the later of the effective date of this Ordinance or the execution of the Financial Agreement by the Entity, the City Clerk's Office shall transmit a certified copy of the Ordinance and Financial Agreement to the Chief Financial Officer of the County and County Counsel for informational purposes.

      16. This ordinance shall take effect upon final passage and publication in accordance with the laws of the State of New Jersey.

STATEMENT

This ordinance grants a long term tax abatement to 54 Lockwood Street Urban Renewal, LLC, c/o Bridge Industrial, One Gatehall Drive, Suite 201, Parsippany, New Jersey 07054, for a Twenty (20) year term for a project located in the East Ward at 54-56 Lockwood St., Newark, New Jersey and identified on the City's tax map as Block 2412, Lot 58 involving the demolition of the existing obsolete industrial buildings, environmental site remediation, and redevelopment of the land with construction of an approximately 211,388 square foot industrial distribution warehouse building consisting of approximately 26 loading docks, 2 drive in ramps, and 155 car parking spaces, all as further described in the Developer's Application, located at 54-56 Lockwood St., Newark, New Jersey and identified on the City's tax map as Block 2412, Lot 58 (collectively, the "Project").

      WHEREAS, the Office of Emergency Management within the Department of Public Safety ("OEM") is committed to providing efficient and effective Citizens' Emergency Alert System to the City of Newark ("City") and its citizens; and 
      
      WHEREAS, pursuant to Local Public Contracts Law, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-5(1)(dd), a contract for the support or maintenance of proprietary computer hardware and software may be awarded without advertising and public bidding; and
      	
      WHEREAS, OEM desires to enter into a contract with Rave Wireless, Inc. ("Rave Wireless"), 50 Speen Street, Suite 301, Framingham, MA 01701, for the provision of maintenance and support of the Citizens' Emergency Alert System, which is Rave Wireless's proprietary software; and
      
      WHEREAS, said contract is essential for the conduct of the affairs of the OEM, as said maintenance and support contract includes, Fully hosted platform operated on the Rave Alert for Public Safety,  NDN(tm) telecom network, Customizable contact management, Unlimited system users, Voice (Recorded or Text-to-Speech with TTY/TDD), Email, Fax, Pager, Social Media, RSS, IPAWS, GIS Mapping, Special Events Manager, NWS Automated Weather Alerts, Rave Mobile  provided Voice Add-On Module, Premium SMS Messaging, Social Media Integration, CAP inbound/outbound, Geopolling, SMS Opt-In, Inbound 800 Service, Smart Loader, Loaded Landlines, Conference Blast, and Rave Prepare live customer support and unlimited live webinar training for use by the City's essential Departments and agencies; and 
      
      WHEREAS, Rave Wireless has represented that it has the exclusive right to provide these goods or services for maintenance and support of proprietary computer hardware and software, and the Coordinator of OEM certifies that said goods and services are essential and necessary for the conduct of the affairs of the Department of Public Safety, N.J.S.A. 40A:11-2(39); and
      
      WHEREAS, the annual cost of this service is expected to be Forty-Eight Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($48,000.00) each year for two (2) years, and should not exceed Ninety-Six Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($96,000.00) over that time period; and
      
      WHEREAS, the Coordinator of OEM has determined and certified in writing that the value of this contract will exceed $53,000.00; and
      
      WHEREAS, this Contract is being awarded pursuant to a "Non-Fair and Open" Process pursuant to State Pay-to-Play Law, N.J.S.A.19:44A-20.5; and 
       
      WHEREAS, Rave Wireless has completed and submitted a Political Contribution Disclosure Form and a Business Entity Disclosure Certification, which certifies that it has not made any reportable contributions to a political or candidate committee in the City of Newark in the previous one (1) year, and the contract will prohibit Rave Wireless from making any reportable contributions throughout the term of the contract; and
      
      WHEREAS, Rave Wireless and its subcontractors, if any, have certified that it and they are in compliance with the City's Contractor Pay-to-Play Reform Ordinance 2:4-22C.
 
      NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE MUNICIPAL COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NEWARK, NEW JERSEY, THAT:

1. The Mayor and/or his designee, and the Business Administrator and the Director of the Department of Public Safety or his designee,  are authorized to enter into and execute a contract with Rave Wireless, Inc., 50 Speen Street, Suite 301, Framingham, MA 01701, to provide support and maintenance of proprietary software and hardware, which includes: Fully hosted platform operated on the Rave Alert for Public Safety,  NDN(tm) telecom network, Customizable contact management, Unlimited system users, Voice (Recorded or Text-to-Speech with TTY/TDD), Email, Fax, Pager, Social Media, RSS, IPAWS, GIS Mapping, Special Events Manager, NWS Automated Weather Alerts, Rave Mobile  provided Voice Add-On Module, Premium SMS Messaging, Social Media Integration, CAP inbound/outbound, Geopolling, SMS Opt-In, Inbound 800 Service, Smart Loader, Loaded Landlines, Conference Blast, and Rave Prepare live customer support and unlimited live webinar training for use by the City's essential Departments.   
                       
2. Said contract shall not exceed Ninety-Six Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($96,000.00) and shall be for the two year period commencing January 1, 2026 and ending on December 31, 2027.

3. This Contract is ratified back from January 1, 2026 through the date of adoption of this authorizing Resolution.

4. Pursuant to N.J.A.C 5:30-5(a), Temporary Budget attached hereto is the Chief Finance Officer's Partial Certification of Funds certifying that funds in the amount of Forty-Eight Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($48,000.00), and are available in the 2026 Budget for the purposes set forth herein and the line appropriation which shall be charged is as follows: Business Unit NW051, Dept. G24, Div./Proj. P24M0, Activity A, Account # 71280, Budget Ref B2024.  

5. This Contract is being awarded pursuant to the Non-Fair and Open Procedures of the State of New Jersey Pay-to-Play Law, (N.J.S.A. 19:44A-20.5), the Local Public Contracts Law, (N.J.S.A. 40A:11-5(1)(dd), and the City of Newark's Contractor Pay-to-Play Reform Ordinance 2:4-22C. There shall be no advance payments made against this contract in accordance with N.J.S.A. 40A:5-16.

6. The Business Entity Disclosure Certification, Political Contribution Disclosure Form, and the Determination of Value Letter are attached in support of this Resolution and shall be placed on file with the Office of the City Clerk by the Director of the Department of Finance.
 	
7. There shall be no amendments or changes to this contract without approval of the Municipal Council.

8. This Contract will contain language prohibiting any contributions in violation of any State or local law.

9. A duly executed copy of the Contract shall be filed in the Office of the City Clerk by the Coordinator of the Office of Emergency Management.

10. A notice of this action shall be published in a newspaper authorized by law to publish a legal advertisement and as required by law within ten (10) days of its passage.


STATEMENT

This Resolution ratifies and authorizes the Mayor and/or his designee, the Business Administrator and the Director of the Department of Public Safety or his Designee, to enter into and execute a contract with Rave Wireless, Inc., 50 Speen Street, Suite 301, Framingham, MA 01701, for the provision of the Citizens' Emergency Alert Mass Notification System for an amount not to exceed $96,000.00, for a two (2) year period commencing January 1, 2026 and ending on December 31, 2027.

      WHEREAS, the City of Newark (the "City") wishes to utilize the State Contract, #T-0126 OEM and Non-OEM, Maintenance and Repair Services for Light/Medium Duty Vehicles, : (1) American Hose & Hydraulics, 700 21st Avenue, Paterson, NJ 07513, (2) On-Site Fleet Service Inc., 36 Edgeboro Road, East Brunswick, NJ 08816, Cliffside Body Corp. 130 Broad Avenue, Fairview, NJ 07022, and (3) Tra-Par Transmissions- 10-16 Greylock Street, Belleville, NJ 07109, authorized vendors thereunder, for the purchase of OEM and Non-OEM maintenance and repair services for an amount not to exceed Six Hundred, Fifty Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($650,000.00), commencing upon approval by the Municipal Council through February 2, 2029 inclusive of any extensions by the State; and

Pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40A:11-12 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 5:34-7.29, the Mayor and/or his designees, and the Business Administrator or the  Qualified Purchasing Agent, are hereby authorized to utilize State Contract T0126 OEM and Non-OEM Maintenance and Repair Services for Light/Medium Duty Vehicles, to enter into and execute contracts with; (1) American Hose & Hydraulics, 700 21st Avenue, Paterson, NJ 07513 , (2) On-Site Fleet Service Inc., 36 Edgeboro Road, East Brunswick, NJ 08816, (3) Cliffside Body Corp. 130 Broad Avenue, Fairview, NJ 07022, and (4)Tra-Par Transmissions- 10-16 Greylock Street, Belleville, NJ 07109, authorized vendors thereunder, for the purchase of OEM and Non-OEM maintenance and repair services for the Department of Water and Sewer Utilities and Department of Public Works/Sanitation in an amount not exceed Six Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars and Zero Cents ($650,000.00) for the period commencing upon approval by the City Municipal Council through February 02, 2029 inclusive of any extensions by the State.

5. There shall be no advance payments of this State Contract in accordance with N.J.S.A. 40A:5-16.
